clue.text: Mum goes round Scottish city briefly, a holy place

indicators.note: the word for mum is wrapped around the shortened city name

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum

indicators.note: briefly means the city's name is cut short, keeping only its familiar opening

parts.note: Edinburgh is the Scottish capital

explanation.surface: A mother tours a Scottish city in a hurry and arrives at a sacred site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the city name short, and 'goes round' wraps the mother word around the remainder; Medina is in Saudi Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia is Islam's second most sacred city, burial place of the Prophet.

clue.text: Evil-looking relation kept outside province

indicators.note: the relation is kept around the province, holding it within

parts.note: a sister is a family relation
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A menacing relative is kept out of a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Province' is a common British name for Northern Ireland; 'kept outside' means the relative surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something threatening or suggesting harm, an ominous appearance.

clue.text: For writer there could be lonely path — or not

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether the road ahead will be solitary or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals an anagram of LONELY PATH OR NOT, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a prolific Victorian novelist, author of the Barsetshire chronicles.

clue.text: A mad girl, not good, bashed officer

indicators.note: bashed suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged
not means the letter for good is left out of the phrase

explanation.surface: A crazed young woman behaving badly attacks a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G from A MAD GIRL leaving AMADIRL, which 'bashed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior commander in the navy, a high-ranking officer.

clue.text: Plain problem for the understocked art gallery

definitions.text: problem for the understocked art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery short of pictures faces a plain difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a gallery with few works offers visitors little to view.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unattractive in appearance, and an empty gallery literally has few exhibits to view.

clue.text: Part of body someone found in club?

explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a part of the body, and someone belonging to a club or society is one of its enrolled people.

clue.text: Deliver a kitchen item maybe

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler delivers the ball, and a basin for mixing is a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Queen, outwardly holy and ethereal female

indicators.note: outwardly means the holy word lies on the outside, wrapping the queen

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or holy
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen with a saintly exterior is a delicate spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (crossword slang for pious) 'outwardly' surrounds ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri in Persian mythology is a beautiful fairy or spirit being.

clue.text: Fellow about to give sign of approval

indicators.note: about means the word for fellow is turned around

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A college fellow is ready to show approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DON round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping the head downward is a gesture of agreement or assent.

clue.text: Old man getting on is in a state

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man getting on in years is in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the United States, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: End at home tucking into Friday fare?

indicators.note: tucking into means the home word is placed inside the fare

parts.note: fish is traditionally eaten on Fridays
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone at home ends the week tucking into a Friday supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Many Christians traditionally eat fish rather than meat on Fridays; 'tucking into' pretends to mean eating but signals an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to bring something to a close or conclusion.

clue.text: I am on the phone, unable to get away

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
mobile is a phone, so being on the mobile is being on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on a call cannot escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Immobile means motionless or fixed in place, so stuck where one is.

clue.text: Point in big race — man can't trot here somehow!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are reshaped in some way into something new

explanation.surface: At a certain point in a big horse race, the rider complains he cannot trot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges MAN CAN'T TROT HERE. The Derby is England's great flat race at Epsom, and this is its famous bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattenham Corner is the sharp bend at Epsom racecourse, a key spot in the Derby.

clue.text: Fish finds sheltered side to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the north means the word is read upwards

parts.note: lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: Fish find shelter on the northern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reverses LEE, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: More than one vegetable goes mouldy at back of vehicle

indicators.note: at back of places the decaying word behind the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
rots means decays or goes mouldy

explanation.surface: Vegetables left in the back of a car are going mouldy.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots are orange root vegetables, the plural matching the definition's several.

clue.text: Notice nothing that should create fuss

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Ignoring a notice should create a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means bother or commotion, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Begin with Latin before English, creating surprise

indicators.note: before places the Latin letter ahead of the English one

parts.note: start means begin

explanation.surface: Starting with Latin ahead of English surprises a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden shock or alarm.

clue.text: Once again root about to see what scientists are up to

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to root about is to search

explanation.surface: Rummaging around once more to see what the lab team are doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists conduct systematic investigation, studying a subject to find new facts.

clue.text: Friendly female taken in by a story

indicators.note: taken in by means the female letter goes inside the story

parts.note: a fable is a story

explanation.surface: A friendly woman is fooled by a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' places F inside A FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means good-natured and easy to talk to, genial.

clue.text: Finish reading the sentence and fail to continue

explanation.surface: A reader reaches the end of a sentence and stops dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a sentence ends with a full stop (US: period).
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching the end-of-sentence mark finishes it, and stopping abruptly means ceasing completely.

clue.text: Man going across Severn estuary

indicators.note: going across means the name spans the two words

explanation.surface: A man wades across the Severn estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'sevERN ESTuary'. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Wild parties — "goer" is getting silly

indicators.note: getting silly suggests the letters are turned into nonsense and rearranged

explanation.surface: A party animal is getting foolish at the revels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting silly' rearranges GOER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgies are riotous gatherings of excess and revelry.

clue.text: Girl cut off before everyone returns

indicators.note: before places the cutting word ahead

parts.note: to prune is to cut off branches

indicators.note: returns means the word for everyone is turned backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A girl is cut off before everyone comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses ALL to LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a female given name.

clue.text: Authentic dance sounds

indicators.note: sounds means the dance word is heard, not written

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Dance music that sounds genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' gives the spoken reel, a Scottish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Real means genuine, not fake.

clue.text: Fruit and egg taken to the mountains

indicators.note: taken to means the egg letter is attached to the mountains

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Fruit and eggs are packed for a trip to the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: O for egg comes from its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Reject amorous advance at university

parts.note: to make a pass is an amorous advance
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student turns down a romantic approach at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up is to decline or turn down an opportunity.

clue.text: Tragic king finally cut down in field

indicators.note: finally cut down means the king's name loses its last letter

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A tragic king is finally struck down in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally cut down' removes the last letter, R, from LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or open grassland.

clue.text: Heartless head cook

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for head is removed

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: A cruel boss is the head cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' drops the central I of CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a kitchen.
